newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares slip marginally in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares slip marginally in quiet trade.

text.p: Egyptian shares fell slightly on Sunday in slow trade as profit-hungry investors hung onto their shares in anticipation of higher prices, brokers said.
The Capital Markets Authority (CMA) overall index closed 0.01 points lower at 235.03 on volume of 66.14 million pounds ($19.45 million).
The registration of newly-privatised Memphis Pharmaceutical and Chemical Industries made up over 50 million pounds of this turnover.

"Investors are expecting the prices to rise so they're holding onto their shares and foreign funds that have bought into the market are keeping their portfolio steady," said Hany El-Beltagy financial advisor at El-Rashad Securities Brokerage.
Eipico/Egyptian International Pharmaceutical Industries consolidated Thursday's gains, jumping 5.00 pounds to close at 150.00 after shares worth 3.99 million pounds traded.
"There is talk about profits and export markets to be opened by the company," Beltagy said.

Suez Cement closed 0.25 pounds up at 47.10 after shares worth 2.92 million pounds changed hands. The firm is still performing well since the National Bank of Egypt said it would sell all or most of the 15 percent it holds in the firm through a GDR.
Egyptian Tora Portland Cement was the best performer in the popular cement sector, rising 2.40 to close at 60.50 in brisk trade.
North Cairo Flour Mills was again one of the bourse's most actively traded firms, with turnover of 1.15 million pounds. But the share ended unchanged at 100.00 pounds.
The CMA index for openly traded firms fell to 348.70 points from 350.39 on Thursday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms crept up to 160.75 from 160.74 points.
